scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: The design covers CI, tests, IaC, blue-green deployment, monitoring, and rollback well; the only unresolved item is the unquantified under-10-minute deployment constraint.

findings.title: Deployment-time target is not explicitly demonstrated
findings.explanation: The architecture has caching, parallelization, and stage timing instrumentation, but it does not state a measured or bounded end-to-end release duration. That leaves the under-10-minute deployment constraint unverified from the submitted evidence.
findings.recommendation: State the expected end-to-end path and show how the combined build, test, approval, and rollout steps are budgeted to remain under 10 minutes, or clarify that this is an assumed operational target rather than a guaranteed SLO.

findings.title: Blue-green rollout and rollback path are well aligned
findings.explanation: Production is modeled as separate blue and green deployments with an active-slot router, readiness checks, and retention of the previous healthy slot for rollback. This directly supports zero-downtime release switching and fast recovery.

findings.title: Promotion gates cover quality, test, security, and approvals
findings.explanation: The pipeline blocks release on test coverage, static analysis, and image scanning, then uses staged environment checks and explicit approvals before production. This is a coherent control chain for CI/CD governance.

results.summary: A coherent Azure streaming design covers multi-source ingestion, SQL-like stream processing, anomaly-driven actions, stateful persistence, and operational monitoring with a credible path for high throughput and low latency.

findings.title: Partitioned streaming path supports the core scale and latency goals
findings.explanation: The ingestion path uses Event Hubs buffering plus a partition-parallel Stream Analytics job, which is an appropriate shape for high-throughput low-latency stream processing.

findings.title: Idempotent downstream actioning reduces duplicate side effects
findings.explanation: The design separates anomaly detection from action publication and uses a deduplicating action handler with a ledger, which is a strong fit for retry-prone event delivery.

findings.title: Operational telemetry is wired into the main services
findings.explanation: Monitoring is attached to Event Hubs, Stream Analytics, Cosmos DB, Event Grid, and both functions, giving direct visibility into backlog, watermarking, retries, throttling, and completion health.

results.summary: The architecture covers the required client, governance, smart contract, off-chain storage, integration, and monitoring paths, but the blockchain platform and consensus choice remain TBD, blocking full validation of BFT, finality, and throughput targets.

findings.title: Consensus mechanism remains undecided
findings.explanation: The network component explicitly leaves the chain, validator count, deployment topology, and consensus algorithm TBD. That is enough to show the architecture intent, but it is not yet a concrete consensus design for a Byzantine-fault-tolerant consortium ledger.
findings.recommendation: Select the target consortium chain and document the consensus protocol, validator membership model, and failure assumptions so the network can be implemented and reviewed against the BFT requirement.

findings.title: Throughput target is not yet backed by a capacity decision
findings.explanation: The design names the 1000+ TPS goal, but the submitted architecture does not yet provide the specific chain selection or topology needed to make that target credible. The requirement is acknowledged, but the capacity strategy is still placeholder-level.
findings.recommendation: Choose a blockchain platform and validator topology that can be benchmarked against the 1000+ TPS target, and document the bottleneck assumptions for contract execution, transaction submission, and finality.

findings.title: Finality target depends on unresolved chain selection
findings.explanation: The architecture says finality under 10 seconds must be achieved, but the selected ledger and consensus mechanism are unspecified. Without that decision, the submitted design cannot yet demonstrate a credible path to the required finality bound.
findings.recommendation: Fix the ledger choice and state the finality model, then validate the expected finality path for the intended membership size and failure model.

findings.title: Implementation path for the consensus network is still too abstract
findings.explanation: The design correctly separates governance, transaction orchestration, and network submission, but the actual blockchain implementation remains a placeholder. That leaves deployment details, validator operations, and chain-specific contract runtime decisions unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Pin the chain/runtime combination, then define deployment steps, validator onboarding, and contract deployment/upgrade mechanics for that platform.

results.summary: The design covers the core conversational bot, multilingual intent/FAQ/sentiment flow, multi-turn state, and conversation telemetry, but channel/language scope and quality targets still need explicit confirmation.

findings.title: Approved channel and language scope need confirmation
findings.explanation: The architecture propagates locale and includes channel adapters, but it does not name the approved language set or the approved external channels. Those remain open decisions rather than fully fixed implementation choices.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the supported languages and approved channels, then map each to a tested adapter/model path and fallback behavior.

findings.title: Quality target needs measured validation
findings.explanation: The evaluation gate and confidence-based routing show a credible strategy toward the >85% accuracy target, but the submission does not include actual evaluation results or a release threshold proving the target is met.
findings.recommendation: Attach an offline evaluation report with per-language intent/entity and FAQ-answer accuracy, plus the promotion rule used to block underperforming versions.

findings.title: Multimodal bot responsibilities are cleanly separated
findings.explanation: The design uses a dedicated media normalization stage, a turn orchestrator, specialized NLU, FAQ retrieval, sentiment, and shared state. This separation makes the responsibilities easy to reason about and keeps the bot boundary replaceable.

results.summary: A coherent confidential-compute MPC design with owner-scoped trust boundaries, attestation-gated key release, encrypted storage, and metadata-only control/telemetry paths.

findings.title: Owner-scoped confidential compute path is well-aligned to zero-exposure processing
findings.explanation: The design keeps raw inputs out of the shared control plane, uses encrypted per-owner storage, and only releases keys after attestation to peers running in confidential VMs. That directly matches the core confidential-computing scope.

findings.title: Attestation-gated secure key release is integrated end to end
findings.explanation: The peer obtains MAA claims and presents them to Key Vault / Managed HSM for policy-validated Secure Key Release, which is a coherent control chain for protecting data in use.

findings.title: Metadata-only logging and monitoring reduce exposure risk
findings.explanation: Monitoring and audit flows are deliberately redacted and exclude payloads, keys, and attestation tokens, which supports confidential-workload operations without leaking sensitive material.

results.summary: A coherent global GCP web architecture with managed runtime, CDN, global load balancing, cache-aside reads, Cloud SQL, and versioned migrations that covers the published core scope.

findings.title: Global edge delivery and traffic management are well aligned
findings.explanation: The architecture places Cloud CDN in front of a Google Cloud Global Load Balancer and uses versioned static assets, which is a strong pattern for global delivery and low-latency reads.

findings.title: Managed data path is coherent
findings.explanation: Cloud SQL is clearly designated as the authoritative relational store, and the release pipeline includes reviewed versioned migrations, which supports safe schema evolution.

findings.title: Operational visibility covers the main failure domains
findings.explanation: Monitoring receives signals from the load balancer, runtime, cache, and database, giving a reasonable basis for health checks and SLO tracking.

results.summary: A coherent GCP batch-and-stream pipeline centered on Pub/Sub, Dataflow/Beam, GCS staging, BigQuery, DLQ replay, and Cloud Monitoring covers the published core scope with strong internal consistency.

findings.title: Unified Beam/Dataflow layer covers both batch and streaming paths
findings.explanation: The design uses a single Dataflow/Apache Beam processing layer for streaming events from Pub/Sub and batch inputs from Cloud Storage. This reduces duplication and keeps transformation logic aligned across modes.

findings.title: Watermarking, late data, and windowing are explicitly addressed
findings.explanation: The processing component description includes event-time windows and late-data handling, and the Pub/Sub-to-Dataflow connection notes watermark tracking. That is a strong fit for event-time batch/stream convergence.

findings.title: Failure handling includes quarantine and controlled replay
findings.explanation: Poison or repeatedly failing records are sent to a durable DLQ and can be replayed after remediation, which is a concrete failure path for the pipeline.

findings.title: Operational telemetry is propagated end-to-end
findings.explanation: Backlog, lag, worker health, sink errors, duplicate/replay counts, and output freshness are all surfaced to Cloud Monitoring, giving the design a coherent observability story.

results.summary: The design covers custom and AutoML training, versioned model promotion, online and batch prediction, monitoring, explanations, and automated retraining with a coherent GCP ML platform flow.

findings.title: Clear separation of online and batch serving
findings.explanation: The design isolates batch scoring from the low-latency online endpoint, reducing contention and keeping each path focused on its own operational profile.

findings.title: Good provenance and release discipline
findings.explanation: Immutable artifact storage plus a gated release pipeline give a strong end-to-end story for reproducibility, rollback, and controlled promotion.

findings.title: Monitoring closes the retraining loop
findings.explanation: Serving telemetry, batch job health, drift indicators, and delayed quality slices are tied back into the release pipeline, which supports ongoing model maintenance.

results.summary: AI review is unavailable. This is a basic structural check of submitted identifiers and endpoints, not an architecture assessment. Numeric fields are compatibility placeholders, not design feedback.

findings.title: Full architecture review unavailable
findings.explanation: The design has not been evaluated against required scope.
findings.recommendation: Retry the AI review when the service is available.

results.summary: The design presents a coherent Anthos-centered multi-cloud Kubernetes platform with centralized fleet management, GitOps reconciliation, separate policy evaluation, service mesh, monitoring, and hybrid connectivity across GKE, AWS, Azure, and on-prem.

findings.title: Unified fleet control plane is clearly established
findings.explanation: The design uses Anthos Fleet Management as the central management boundary and connects it to every target environment, which cleanly matches the multi-cloud Kubernetes management scope.

findings.title: Configuration drift and policy evaluation are separated well
findings.explanation: Config Sync handles desired-state reconciliation while Anthos Config Management policies report policy findings separately, making drift and violations easier to reason about and operate.

findings.title: Security boundary is layered across identity, policy, and mesh
findings.explanation: Scoped operator/workload identity, RBAC, audit logging, and service-mesh mTLS/trust controls form a coherent security model for multi-cloud access and workload communication.

findings.title: Operational visibility spans fleet, policy, mesh, and connectivity
findings.explanation: Monitoring ingests fleet state, cluster health, policy findings, mesh signals, and latency measurements, which is well aligned with the platform’s operational scope.

results.summary: A coherent GCP analytics pipeline streams events through Pub/Sub into BigQuery, serves interactive SQL dashboards, and uses scheduled idempotent refreshes with monitoring for latency, freshness, and cost.

findings.title: Pub/Sub buffering protects BigQuery from ingest bursts
findings.explanation: The event stream is absorbed by Pub/Sub before reaching the ingestion handler, which gives the design a clear decoupling point for short consumer or warehouse slowdowns and supports the high-ingest target.

findings.title: Query path is tuned for dashboard responsiveness
findings.explanation: Partitioning, clustering, query byte caps, and p95 latency monitoring form a coherent strategy for interactive SQL over large datasets.

findings.title: Refresh and freshness are explicitly operationalized
findings.explanation: Cloud Scheduler, an idempotent refresh worker, and freshness monitoring make the automatic refresh behavior concrete rather than implied.

results.summary: The pipeline is strong for large-scale ingest, transcoding, thumbnailing, adaptive delivery, and monitoring, but the DRM path and its operationalization remain under-specified for full core-scope completion.

findings.title: DRM protection remains unresolved
findings.explanation: The architecture includes a DRM placeholder, but it explicitly leaves encryption mode, license flow, key policy, and device matrix unresolved. Because DRM protection is part of the core scope, the design still lacks a concrete, implementable protection flow.
findings.recommendation: Select a specific DRM scheme and define packaging, license issuance, key management, and playback entitlement behavior before implementation.

findings.title: Implementation path for protected delivery is still incomplete
findings.explanation: The protected playback path depends on owner-approved DRM and entitlement decisions that are not yet fixed. Without a concrete vendor/protocol choice and end-to-end license flow, the design cannot be directly implemented for secure delivery of protected outputs.
findings.recommendation: Finalize the DRM vendor and license service integration, then document how the CDN serves only entitled protected assets.

findings.title: Under-2x real-time constraint is not fully operationalized
findings.explanation: The design exposes encoding elapsed-time telemetry, but the metric definition and aggregation basis for proving the under-2x real-time constraint are explicitly deferred. That leaves the performance constraint unoperationalized for mixed media workloads, especially 4K/HDR inputs.
findings.recommendation: Define the exact measurement method for source duration versus end-to-end encoding time and set the aggregation policy used for 4K/HDR jobs.

findings.title: Core scope is not fully complete until DRM is specified
findings.explanation: DRM is a published core requirement, but the submission leaves it as a TBD integration rather than a concrete design choice. This is a requirements coverage gap, not just an optional extension.
findings.recommendation: Provide the actual DRM packaging, license, and entitlement design so the core media protection path is specified end to end.
